newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline fall on weaker crude and slack demand.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline fall on weaker crude and slack demand.

text.p: NWE gasoline prices fell on Tuesday as international crude prices sank and buyers remained elusive, traders said.
"The market's sloppy at the moment," said one trader. "There's not too much demand out."
On the barge market, a Eurograde barge was done at $202 fob ARA in late trade. Bids and offers were reported around $199/$203 fob ARA.
A Eurograde barge was done at $206.25 fob ARA in early trade, but many players commented the buyer appeared to be protecting a swaps position.
"I wouldn't be surprised if the buyer in question sold it back in a P&C deal later on," said one trader. "They do this every day to get the quotes as high as possible."
Some players speculated that the buyer was collecting barges for the Middle East market.
Some traders said the barge market could come under increasing downward pressure over the next two weeks as sellers tried to off-load winter spec material before the end of March.
On the cargo market, prices were difficult to guage in the current choppy environment.
"I'd put Eurograde cargoes around $5 under the barges but that might be a bit pessimistic," said one trader.
Traders said a German trader picked up a summer spec cargo for around $212-$213 cif NWE on Monday, but they said prices for such material would be considerably lower now.
Players took little comfort form data released on Tuesday showing that European gasoline inventories in February were well below year-ago levels.

Stichting Euroilstock data showed gasoline inventories rose 1.45 million barrels, or 0.9 percent, in February to 166.05 million barrels, but were 7.21 million barrels, or 4.2 percent, lower than year-ago levels.
"Crude's down and that's the important thing as long as crude stays down there's no way gasoline can push much higher," sid one trader.
